page: Microsoft Azure D16d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, offering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB, providing a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Integrated storage is provisioned as a direct 644 GB local SSD. No dedicated GPUs are included in this server profile.

Benchmark results place the D16d_v5 consistently within the middle 50% tier across multi-threaded and single-threaded compute evaluations. Single-core processing reaches a Geekbench score of 1537.0 and a stress-ng metric of 1898.68, while multi-core workloads deliver 9098.0 in Geekbench and 15521.76 in stress-ng. The system scored 21133.57 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory throughput demonstrates 79.96 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 38.08 GB/sec for writes. The hardware includes AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets alongside hardware cryptography acceleration, delivering 15.33 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.85 GB/sec static web throughput.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with local fast SSD storage balances processing power with temporary data persistence. Workloads requiring extreme GPU acceleration or high RAM-to-vCPU ratios will find this configuration constrained. However, for continuous web application serving, mid-sized relational database hosting, container cluster nodes, and software build pipelines requiring high-speed temporary scratch space, the server provides balanced resource density and dependable compute output.

It delivers 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector support, cryptographic instructions, and an included 644 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch storage. Benchmarks place the system in the median tier across single-core (1537.0 Geekbench) and multi-core (9098.0 Geekbench, 21133.57 PassMark CPU) tasks, achieving 15.33 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.85 GB/sec in static web serving. The balanced allocation between CPU, memory, and local disk makes this server suitable for production application servers, containerized workloads, databases, and CI/CD pipelines.
